design_rationale:
WORKLOG — host_payout_desk task 1 (Desmond Halvorsen, Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule)

STEP 0 — DRAW, SCOPE SNAPSHOT AND DESIGN THESIS
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0015_car_sharing_marketplace/tasks/host_payout_desk --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 4]}
So this task is a tree of two problems with one prerequisite, and its computations carry 5 and 4
factors: payouts_ext_schedule_qualification 5, payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery 4.
Already occupied by task 0: payouts_ext_recovery_correction, payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release and
payouts_ext_requested_draw, with post_recovery_correction_f20745c1, release_claim_reserve_fb50cb2e
and release_host_payout_draw_8e4fb8ab — the correcting entry, the reserve release and the host's own
draw. This task claims two subjects task 0 never touches, the deduction (payouts_deduction_posted)
and the schedule change (payouts_schedule_changed), with two fresh tools. Nothing overlaps, and with
the two tasks together the difficulty's five extended policies are all claimed, each by exactly one
task.

Design thesis. The customer's surface goal is "move me onto a proper settlement rhythm, whatever my
record entitles me to"; he deliberately names no schedule. The scored core parameter is the name of
the schedule he moves onto — the highest-ranked one whose qualifying monthly earnings, qualifying
settled trips and qualifying tenure he all meets. Between the goal and that name the policy puts one
problem he never mentions: the account stands short of money the marketplace is owed after a guest
charged back a trip, and until the recovery is taken against that entry the deductions netted into
his qualifying earnings are not what they will be. The name is decided in parallel by a
twenty-three-month ledger, by which window each of five ladders selects, by how long the payout
account has been open, by the counts of correcting entries and of returned transfers, and by the
standing of his protection enrolment in another difficulty. Terminal state: one new deduction on the
ledger with the account's available balance moved by it, and the schedule field of the account
changed by the customer himself.

STEP 0 CARD A — BASE-INVARIANT CARD
payouts_deduction_posted (the recovery). Governing base policy: payouts_evt_deductions, whose
  eligibility list is empty, so what is inherited is its scope rather than a gate: money the host
  owes is taken from the account rather than invoiced, each deduction names the basis it was taken
  on, a deduction may take the balance below zero, and a deduction posted in error is corrected by a
  correcting entry and never by editing the entry that was wrong. The recovery here obeys all four.
  The base sentence that fixes the recovery share and the grace period is named in this policy's
  overwrite, so its own recovery-share ladder and its recovery inside the grace period are both
  licensed. payouts_evt_earnings is referenced as input lineage; its subject is
  payouts_earning_posted, so it governs no gate here.
payouts_schedule_changed (the move). Governing base policy: payouts_schedule_change. Gate
  schedule_change_notice_elapsed, kind time. Anchor event "the notice is recorded", anchor source
  payouts_accounts.next_payout_date, relation not_before, duration
  params.schedule_change_effective_days (7 on the Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule), unit calendar
  days, counting rule "counted in whole calendar days from the day the notice is taken, with the day
  of notice itself not counted", boundary inclusive. The account records the notice at 2026-08-25;
  plus seven whole days, the day of notice not counted, is 2026-09-01, and the handling date of
  2026-09-17 is not before it, so the change may take effect. Positive and negative boundary cases
  are in solvability_contract.temporal_feasibility.
  Three base clauses this policy handles differently are each named in its overwrite and no wider:
  payouts_schedule_change's qualification sentence, replaced by the highest-ranked-schedule rule;
  payouts_schedule_change's "the move takes effect on a future date rather than the day it is asked
  for" sentence, replaced by a sentence that records the move once the schedule's effective period
  has run, which leaves the inherited notice gate in force and agrees with it; and
  payouts_account_opening's sentence fixing tenure from the day the member profile was opened and
  the settled trip count over the whole life of the account, replaced by a sentence that fixes the
  qualifying tenure from the day the payout account was opened and the qualifying settled trips from
  the trip earnings the account itself carries. Those two quantities are the only ones a payouts
  compute can read at all — there is no primitive that reaches the member profile — so the deviation
  is declared rather than silently taken.
Inherited and untouched: payouts_agg_multi_holding (one account per host — the seed has exactly
one), payouts_holds (hold_reason is none), payouts_evt_transfer (no transfer is made in this task),
payouts_closure (the account is not closed).

STEP 0 CARD B — BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
  recovery -> the chargeback entry of 2026-09-08, named by source_ledger_id. Excluded from the same
    basis: the six marketplace commissions, which are ordinary trip deductions and left nothing
    outstanding, and the six transfers, which moved money the host was entitled to at the time.
    There is exactly one entry on the chargeback recovery basis, so the correlation is one entry to
    one recovery and no aggregation scope is leaned on.
  schedule move -> the account itself, named by payout_account_id; the host holds one account.
Already settled by existing rows: nothing on this account has been corrected — there is no
adjustment entry at all, which is why the twelve-month flows are deductions alone.

STEP 0 CARD C — PROBLEM-TREE CARD
  payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery (B, agent, post_balance_recovery_b10514b8)
      ^ value_input on net_flows_year
  payouts_ext_schedule_qualification    (A, ROOT, user, change_host_payout_schedule_75a33b7a)
Edge A<-B. Form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from A's own rule: "The schedule a host moves
  onto is settled only once every ground on which the account stands short of money the marketplace
  is owed carries the recovery entry taken against it." Four-point test: (1) the connective is "only
  once" and the sentence runs in the affirmative direction, which is how this desk states a standing
  it will fix once the account is square; its exact contrapositive, "the schedule a host moves onto
  is not settled before every ground on which the account stands short of money the marketplace is
  owed carries the recovery entry taken against it", adds, drops and splits nothing, and the
  difficulty's charter carries both directions, the draw of task 0 being stated negatively; (2) the
  XX side is a record-visible state — an entry that has left the account short, and the recovery
  entry taken against it, in the words find_payouts_ledger returns; (3) no tool, no policy id, no
  snake_case, no row id; (4) hard strength, scope exactly the closed set of grounds on which the
  account stands short, matching the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a
  recovery entry taken against an earlier entry: payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery; the other
  writes book a correcting entry, a reserve release and a transfer. Derivation: the sentence says the
  move waits on the recovery; the records show a chargeback of 4820.00 booked 2026-09-08 with no
  entry naming it and an available balance of -1310.00; the recovery policy's own rule says what its
  write books and that it is the write that books it; therefore the recovery comes first. Resolved
  by post_balance_recovery_b10514b8, owner agent.
Topological order: B, A. A two-node chain, so there is nothing to reorder.
Customer's own write: A. The settlement arrangement on the host's own account is his to set, and the
agent unlocks the change and hands it over.

STEP 1 — POLICIES
payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery overwrites one clause of payouts_evt_deductions — base fixed
  that the marketplace recovers the schedule's share of each later earning once a grace period has
  run, and extended fixes what that share is, which earnings count as later, how much stands short
  and how much of it the protection enrolment carries rather than the host. Trigger state_due.
  Its rule now states the anchor its clock runs from — "counted in whole calendar days from the day
  of the most recent entry on which money charged back by a guest was taken off the account" — so
  compute invents no basis the prose withholds.
payouts_ext_schedule_qualification overwrites three clauses, listed in Card A. Trigger on_request.
Forward references: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, chooses or rounds quotes its
rule sentence verbatim in compute_basis, and each ladder binding quotes the whole tier sentence.
Reverse sweep: every load-bearing sentence of both rules is claimed — the window sentences by the
window bindings, the tier sentences by the ladder bindings, the ordering sentence of the
qualification ("The offset and the two set-asides are each worked out on the qualifying monthly
earnings as first measured rather than one upon the other ...") by the qualifying_earnings binding,
the floor-testing sentence by the result binding, and the rounding sentences by the RND in each. The
offset sentence now says in terms which way the net moves the figure — "because deductions are
booked as negative entries and corrections as positive ones, that net lowers the qualifying monthly
earnings whenever deductions outweigh corrections and lifts them whenever corrections outweigh
deductions" — which is exactly the signed addition the compute performs. No window is described as
"the statement month": every rolling one-month window is written "the month up to that day", which
is what within_months=1 computes.

STEP 2 — TOOL CARDS
post_balance_recovery_b10514b8 (agent, write). Object: one payout ledger entry and the account it is
  booked to. Atomic action: book one deduction naming the entry it is taken against, and lower the
  account's available balance by the sum taken. Change: a negative entry on the chargeback recovery
  basis with today's date and the month it is reported in; the earlier entry is untouched.
  Observable: the recovery as its own line on the statement and the balance down by that sum.
  Receipt: the new deduction's reference, the earlier entry's reference and the sum.
change_host_payout_schedule_75a33b7a (user, write). Object: the payout account. Atomic action: set
  the schedule the account settles under. Change: payout_schedule_name becomes the named schedule;
  everything already owed stays as it stands. Observable: the new schedule on the account summary.
  Receipt: the account reference and the schedule now in force. Its two parameters are both things
  the customer holds before acting — the account reference the agent has read back to him and the
  schedule name the agent has told him.
The recovery tool keeps the identity the charter declares between the ledger and available_balance,
so what its docstring promises is what its body performs. Neither validates a prerequisite; see
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.
Gate run: .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_task_tools.py $DIFF ->
TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK.

STEP 3 — WORLD
One host, one payout account, thirty-four ledger entries spanning 2024-11 to 2026-09, one protection
enrolment and three claim records. Why each class exists:
  twenty-one trip earnings — fourteen inside the twelve-month window give the qualifying earnings
    basis of 655.00 a month and the qualifying trip count of 14; seven older ones, 2024-11-06 to
    2025-08-19, are outside it and are the near miss for both, as well as making the account's long
    history coherent. Two of the fourteen fall in the month up to the handling day, which is what
    the earnings and trips baselines fall back to.
  six marketplace commissions — the ordinary deduction side of the trips, and part of the
    twelve-month flows netted into the qualifying earnings.
  one chargeback of 4820.00 booked 2026-09-08 — the entry that left the account short, the entry the
    recovery names, the reason the shortfall ladder nets the whole account rather than a window, and
    the reason the short-account set-aside applies. Delete it and the account is in credit, the
    shortfall measure has nothing to bite on and the prerequisite disappears.
  six transfers out — they are what make the account's netting negative once the chargeback lands,
    and the two inside three months are what put the later-earnings ladder and the monthly-earnings
    ladder on their first tiers. Delete the 2026-08-20 transfer and both ladders fall a tier.
  no adjustment entry and no returned transfer anywhere — these absences are load-bearing: they put
    the offset ladder on its full share and leave the twelve-month flows to the deductions alone.
  the enrolment and its three claim records — the plan in force and the liability finding on the
    most recent appraisal decide the share of the shortfall the host bears; the suspension reason
    together with that appraisal falling inside twelve months decides the cover-standing reduction;
    and the older appraisal of 2025-04-18 carries a host-at-fault finding and lies outside the
    twelve-month window, so it is the near miss on the cross-difficulty side twice over. The
    enrolment carries no liability owed, so it is squarely in the standing the hostplan charter
    describes for an active enrolment.
Prerequisite falsification: the chargeback stands with no entry naming it through its source entry,
and the account carries an available balance of -1310.00. Both are recorded with row paths and
values in prerequisite_closure.
Automatic-clause check: the account is active with hold_reason none and its tax documentation on
file, so no hold, no suspension and no withholding is running; there is no reserve on the account at
all, so no release is owed; no transfer is in flight; the enrolment is active with no suspension
reason and nothing owed, so nothing in the other difficulty is lit either. No cache is deliberately
falsified: available_balance of -1310.00 and reserve_balance of 0.00 are exactly the netting of their
own account deltas at the opening, and the recovery moves the first by the sum it takes, so they are
still exact at the terminal state.

STEP 4 — PERSONA
Desmond speaks like someone who has thought about it first: dry, brief, impatient with detail he did
not ask for, and deliberately silent about which schedule he wants. Volunteered at the opening: that
he is paid as each trip finishes, that the scatter of small amounts is a nuisance to reconcile, that
he wants a proper rhythm today, that he will not name one, and — in passing, making nothing of it —
that nothing has reached his bank for about four weeks, which is true of the seed, the last transfer
being 2026-08-20. Given only when asked: his name, his mobile 7815550198, his billing ZIP 02143, how
long he has listed, that his cars sit under a middle Keyturn Shield plan, that there was a claim in
the summer he left with Keyturn, and a loose five-to-seven-hundred a month from his spreadsheet.
Reacted to only after the agent says something: "fine, get on with it" when told something must be
put straight first, one question about whether the named schedule really is the best the record
allows, and making the change himself when it is handed across. He never mentions a chargeback, a
shortfall or a recovery, never asks whether something has to be sorted first, and his last reaction
answers the last gold action and stops.

STEP 5 — VERIFICATION
Harness: the same build_env/eval_compute/substitute from check_compute.py driven over the replayed
gold. Output actually obtained:
  payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery result 1703.00  baseline 680.00  history rows 34  branches 14
     factor baselines: shortfall_recovery_share 7598.00, later_earnings_measure 0.00,
     shortfall_measure 887.00, host_bearing_of_shortfall 1965.00
  payouts_ext_schedule_qualification    result "Keyturn Weekly Batch Payout Schedule"
     baseline "Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule"  history rows 35  branches 17
     factor baselines: monthly_earnings_measure "Keyturn Express Payout Schedule",
     flows_offset_share "Keyturn Express Payout Schedule",
     cover_standing_reduction "Keyturn Express Payout Schedule",
     short_account_setaside "Keyturn Express Payout Schedule",
     settled_trips_measure "Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule"
Every factor moves its result, and each whole baseline differs from gold. Prerequisite sensitivity,
same harness with the depended-on call skipped: the schedule without the recovery is the Keyturn
Express Payout Schedule rather than the Keyturn Weekly Batch Payout Schedule, because the
twelve-month flows are -6000.00 instead of -7703.00 and the qualifying earnings 506.75 instead of
492.56, which is the difference between clearing the express earnings floor of 500.00 and falling
short of it by 7.44. The edge bears weight.

STEP 6 — EVALUATION AND CLOSURE
Reads: the member lookup and the in-session identity check; the payout account (schedule, state, tax
documentation, next sweep date, opening date, balances); the whole ledger (every aggregate of both
computations, and the chargeback that shows the prerequisite unmet); the protection enrolment (plan,
suspension reason); the claim records (the appraisal that carries the liability finding and the older
one that must be excluded). Writes in topological order: the recovery, then the schedule change
through unlock_user_discoverable_tool -> call_user_discoverable_tool. Closure:
payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery -> recovery_amount -> post_balance_recovery_b10514b8 -> step 7;
payouts_ext_schedule_qualification -> payout_schedule_name -> change_host_payout_schedule_75a33b7a ->
step 9. charter_scope, required_documents and the computation policy ids are the same two ids in the
same order. Nothing in the tree waits on a real-world event.

THE PLACES A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM
  Moving him to the fastest schedule he could name — the rule settles the highest-ranked schedule
    whose three floors are all met, and 14 trips and 492.56 a month clear only the weekly one.
  Reading the qualifying earnings off the last month, 680.00, or off the account summary — the rule
    measures them over twelve months and divides, then takes the offset and the two set-asides off.
  Counting the seven earnings of 2024-11 to 2025-08 — all are twelve whole months or more back.
  Taking the host-at-fault finding from the 2025-04-18 appraisal, or counting that appraisal toward
    the cover-standing reduction — the rule reads the most recent appraisal for the finding and only
    the twelve months up to today for the count.
  Recovering the whole shortfall, or the whole of the later earnings — the early recovery share is
    0.25 and the enrolment carries 262.00 of what stands short.
  Settling the schedule before the recovery is booked — that is the prerequisite, and it is worth a
    whole schedule band.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
Working only from the prose that will be published, the tool schemas, what the finders return and
what Desmond actually says, with the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier masked:
the request is a schedule move on the host's own account, so the act is his. The qualification rule
says the schedule is settled only once every ground on which the account stands short carries its
recovery entry, and the ledger shows a chargeback of 4820.00 with none, so the recovery comes first.
Recovery: the balance has stood short nine days, inside the fourteen-day grace, so the early share of
0.25 on the later earnings; two transfers in three months put the later earnings at the twelve-month
figure of 7860.00, giving 1965.00; money charged back stands on the account so the whole account is
netted, -1310.00, leaving 1310.00 short, of which the host bears 0.80 on a Shield 85 plan with a
guest-at-fault finding, so the enrolment carries 262.00; 1965.00 - 262.00 = 1703.00. Qualification:
monthly basis 655.00; flows of -7703.00 at the full offset share over twelve months, 64.19; the
enrolment stands in good order with one appraisal in the year, so 65.50 is set aside; money charged
back inside three months on an account netting below nothing sets aside a further 32.75; 655.00 -
64.19 - 65.50 - 32.75 = 492.56. Trips 14, tenure 926 days from the day the payout account was
opened. Testing downwards: reserve-backed, fleet and instant all fail on earnings and trips; express
fails on the 500.00 earnings floor by 7.44; weekly is met on 3 trips and 30 days. The schedule is the
Keyturn Weekly Batch Payout Schedule. The draft agrees with gold in value, shape, moment and order.

REVISION 2 — what the source-layer audit found, and what changed
Recorded as symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run result.
  T1-1 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, tenure_anchor an unreal ladder whose fall-through is the published
    baseline). Symptom: the ladder offered a host of two and a half years 926, 23 or 12 days, the
    fall-through measuring tenure from his most recent trip earning so that trading more made him
    newer, and its tier-2 condition — the state of the tax documentation — bore on nothing about how
    long he had traded. Root cause: a factor invented on a quantity the base charter already defines
    and that no payouts compute can read at its source. Change: the ladder is gone; the qualifying
    tenure is now a plain binding, the whole calendar days from the day the payout account was
    opened, and the deviation from base's member-profile anchor is declared in the policy's
    overwrite together with the settled-trip measure. Its place among the five factors is taken by
    short_account_setaside, a share of the qualifying earnings set aside while the account stands
    short after a guest chargeback, whose three tiers rest on the chargeback entries and on the
    netting of the account. Re-run: qualifying tenure 926, qualifying earnings 492.56, and the five
    factor baselines are Express, Express, Express, Express and Standard.
  T1-2 / F-TOOL-1 (the docstring promised a balance movement the body did not perform). Change: the
    recovery tool now lowers available_balance by the sum it takes. Re-run: after the gold recovery
    the account reads -3013.00, which is exactly the netting of the ledger behind it, and the edge
    proof no longer cites a field that moves the other way.
  T1-3 / F-EQ-1 ("the statement month up to that day"). Change: every rolling one-month window in
    the extended charter is written "the month up to that day". Re-run: the published baseline of
    the recovery is 680.00 on one reading and no other.
  F-OV-6 and F-OV-7 (observations: tenure and settled trips defined differently from base). Change:
    both are now covered by one declared overwrite on payouts_account_opening quoting the sentence
    that fixes them and replacing it with the sentence this policy actually applies.
  F-OV-8 (observation: the notice and effective-date machinery neither followed nor overridden).
    Change: base's "the move takes effect on a future date rather than the day it is asked for" is
    now named in the overwrite and replaced by a sentence that records the move once the schedule's
    effective period has run, which agrees with the inherited notice gate rather than contradicting
    it; the gate itself is untouched and still carries the task's temporal_feasibility entry.
  F-EQ-4 (observation: "set against" implemented as a signed addition). Change: the rule now says
    which way the net moves the figure and why, matching the compute exactly.
  F-EQ-5 (observation: no anchor for "how long the balance has stood short"). Change: the rule now
    states the anchor the compute uses.
  F-FAC-3 (observation: settled_trips_measure divided on whether a correcting entry had been
    booked). Change: the ladder now divides on how long the payout account has been open, which is
    what makes a short trading record worth annualising, and its fall-through counts the month
    alone. Re-run: tier 1 taken at 926 days, baseline 2 trips, which settles the entry schedule.
  F-FAC-4 (observation: enrolment_standing_reduction not multi-source and its tier-2 state one the
    hostplan charter says does not persist). Change: the factor is now cover_standing_reduction,
    whose tiers read the enrolment's suspension ground and a count over its claim records — two
    distinct records — and no tier asks for an active enrolment carrying an unpaid liability; the
    seeded enrolment carries none.
  O1-6 needs no change: corrections_year is still 0 and the two anchors for the shortfall clock
    still coincide, and both are now stated in prose either way.

REVISION 3 — re-verification after the round-2 audit
  This task carried no red light out of revision 2 and none of its two policies
  (payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery, payouts_ext_schedule_qualification) was touched this round:
  the charter edits of revision 3 fall entirely in payouts_ext_recovery_correction,
  payouts_ext_claim_reserve_release and payouts_ext_requested_draw, which belong to task 0.
  The stale-figure sweep described in task 0's revision-3 log was run over this file as well, on the same
  basis: every money-shaped figure asserted in an argument_uniqueness_tracing, an objective, a necessity,
  a business_effect, an action_semantics, a stage_provenance fact, a boundary_check, a seed_consistency
  check, a why_false, a flips_to_true_by, an evidence path, a skipped_effect, an order_uniqueness, a
  factor_trace line or this dossier, checked against the figures the world and the derivation actually
  produce. It flagged one figure, 64.19, in three places — the offset amount, which is
  RND(-7703.00 x 0.10 / 12, 2) — and that figure was confirmed correct by reading the binding directly;
  the sweep's closure was then extended to cover division by twelve and by three, after which it flags
  nothing in this file. No figure of this task was carried over from an earlier revision.
user_scenario:
Desmond Halvorsen is forty-six, a systems technician at a hospital in Somerville, and he has been
running four cars on Keyturn since the spring of 2024 as a deliberate second income rather than a
hobby. He keeps a spreadsheet, he knows what each car brings in, and he talks like someone who has
thought about this before he picked up the phone: measured, a little dry, and impatient with being
told things he already knows. He calls the marketplace "Keyturn" and his cars "the fleet", half
joking.

His reason for ringing is about the rhythm of the money rather than any one payment. At the moment
Keyturn pays him out as each trip finishes, so his bank statement is a scatter of small amounts, and
he says it is a nuisance to reconcile against the spreadsheet. He wants to be moved onto a proper
settlement rhythm and he wants it done today. He is careful not to name one: he says he does not
know what the options are called and he does not want to be sold the fastest one, he wants whatever
his trading record actually entitles him to, and he asks the agent to work that out and tell him.
If the agent asks whether he has a preference, he repeats that he has none and that the record
should decide it, and if the agent offers to talk him through all six he declines and says just
tell me which one I qualify for.

He mentions in passing, without making anything of it, that nothing has come through to his bank for
about four weeks now and he had assumed that was simply how the current arrangement worked. He does
not ask about it, does not tie it to his request, and if the agent does not raise it he never
returns to it.

He is content for the agent to look through the account and tidy up anything that needs tidying —
if the agent asks, he says yes, do what you need to do, and does not ask what it is. What he keeps
for himself is the change to the account: he says the settlement arrangement on his own account is
his to set, and when the agent has worked out which schedule the record entitles him to, tells him
the name and hands the change across, he makes it himself and reads back what the confirmation
says.

Asked who he is, he gives his name, Desmond Halvorsen. For confirmation he offers the mobile
Keyturn has for him, 7815550198, and, if a second thing is wanted, the ZIP code on his billing
address, 02143. He has his licence in his wallet and will read the number out if asked for something
else instead. He has no idea what his Keyturn member reference is and says so.

He answers questions plainly and briefly. Asked how long he has been listing, he says since the
spring of 2024. Asked about protection, he says all four cars sit under a Keyturn Shield plan and he
believes it is one of the middle ones. Asked whether anything is outstanding on the protection side
he says he could not swear to it, that there was a claim in the summer on the estate, and that he
left it with Keyturn to settle. Asked how much he earns a month he says it varies and quotes the
spreadsheet loosely, between five and seven hundred, and adds that the agent will have better
figures than he does.

He reacts rather than leads. If the agent tells him something has to be put straight on the account
before the schedule can move, he says fine, get on with it, and asks how long it will take. If the
agent tells him the record puts him on a particular schedule, he asks once whether that is really
the best the record allows, accepts the answer he is given, and does not haggle. If the agent were
to tell him nothing can be changed, he would sound put out and ask when it could be looked at again,
but he would not argue policy.

Once he has made the change himself and heard the confirmation naming the schedule now in force, he
is done. He says that is what he wanted, thanks the agent and rings off, asking for nothing further.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the one member profile matching the name and mobile number the caller states, and read back his member reference, the date his profile was opened and the side of the marketplace he acts on.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the member reference the payout account cannot be located, and both writes are scoped to this host.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record an in-session identity check against the profile using the two details the caller offers, the mobile number and the billing ZIP code.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing that touches a payout may be done before this check has passed, and this call both takes money off the account and changes how it settles.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host's single payout account: the schedule it settles under, its state, the day it was opened, the date it records as its next sweep, the state of the tax documentation and the balances.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The schedule name decides every ladder that asks how the account settles, the tax documentation state and the opening date decide the qualifying tenure, the next sweep date is the anchor of the schedule-change time gate, and the account reference scopes both writes.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull every entry booked to the account: the twenty-one trip earnings, the six marketplace commissions, the money charged back by a guest on 8 September and the six transfers already sent.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every aggregate of both computations reads these rows — the later earnings and the shortfall the recovery is worked out from, and the qualifying earnings, trips and flows the schedule is settled on; their dates also decide which window each ladder selects, and the chargeback standing without a recovery is what shows the prerequisite unmet.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the host protection enrolment: the plan in force, whether it is suspended and on what ground, and the liability still owed on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan in force decides the share of the shortfall the host bears, and the suspension ground together with the liability owed decides the part of the qualifying earnings set aside.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the claim records on that enrolment: the summer filing, its repair-shop appraisal, and the older wheel claim appraised the year before.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The liability finding on the most recent appraisal decides the bearing share; the older appraisal carries the opposite finding and is the record that must be excluded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden recovery tool so that it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the database and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Take the recovery against the money charged back on 8 September out of what the account has since earned, so that what the marketplace is owed stops standing open on the account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: payouts_ext_negative_balance_recovery is the only policy that computes recovery_amount, and its figure is forced by the early recovery share on the twelve-month later earnings less the part of the shortfall the protection enrolment carries.

Basis: the payout account lookup returns exactly one account for this host, and the charter states verbatim 'A host settles through one payout account and one only, however many vehicles they list'. argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_ledger_id: Value 19ffa711-d93e-40d6-a81b-0a5b36e43792. Basis: the ledger read returns this entry with entry_basis 'chargeback_recovery' and entry_date 2026-09-08, and the base rule states verbatim 'A chargeback a guest raises is held against the host at the schedule's chargeback share while it is disputed, and where the dispute is lost the marketplace recovers it inside the schedule's recovery window; where it is won the hold is released in full.' Uniqueness: exactly one entry on the account stands on the chargeback recovery basis; the six marketplace commissions are ordinary trip deductions that left nothing outstanding, and the six transfers moved money the host was entitled to when they were sent.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.recovery_amount: Value 1703.00. The account is swept as each trip completes and the money charged back was booked on 2026-09-08, nine days before the handling date, so the balance has stood short for no longer than the fourteen-day grace period and the early recovery share of 0.25 applies. Two transfers have left the account in the three months up to 2026-09-17, on 2026-06-28 and 2026-08-20, so the later earnings are the trip earnings of the twelve months up to that day: fourteen entries totalling 7860.00, the seven earnings of 2024-11-06 to 2025-08-19 falling outside. A quarter of 7860.00 is 1965.00. Money charged back by a guest stands on the account, so what stands short is the whole account netted: 13060.00 of earnings less 6000.00 of deductions less 8370.00 of transfers is -1310.00, so 1310.00 stands short. The most recent appraisal made under the enrolment, of 2026-07-16, found the loss to be the guest fault and the plan in force is the Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan, so the host bears 0.80 of it, 1048.00, and the enrolment carries the remaining 262.00, which is not recovered. 1965.00 less 262.00 is 1703.00.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_account_id: Value 4f786106-e2c0-4d56-80c3-a442fa3fcd12. Basis: the payout account lookup returns exactly one account for this host, and the charter states verbatim 'A host settles through one payout account and one only, however many vehicles they list'. argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_schedule_name: Value 'Keyturn Weekly Batch Payout Schedule'. The account is swept as each trip completes and two transfers have left it in the three months up to 2026-09-17, so the qualifying monthly earnings are the twelve-month trip earnings of 7860.00 divided by twelve, 655.00. No transfer has come back unpaid in that period, so the full offset share of 0.10 applies: the deductions and corrections of the twelve months, which once the recovery of 1703.00 is booked come to -7703.00, spread over twelve months at that share, take 64.19. The protection enrolment stands in good order and one claim has been appraised under it in the last twelve months, so the claim reduction share of 0.10 sets aside 65.50 of the 655.00; the appraisal of 2025-04-18 falls outside that window. Money charged back by a guest was booked to the account on 2026-09-08, inside the last three months, and the netting of every entry on the account stands below nothing, so the short-account set-aside share of 0.05 sets aside a further 32.75. The qualifying monthly earnings are therefore 655.00 less 64.19 less 65.50 less 32.75, which is 492.56. The payout account has been open since 2024-03-05, 926 days, a year or longer, so the qualifying settled trips are the fourteen trip earnings of the last twelve months and the qualifying tenure is those 926 days. Testing the six schedules downwards: the reserve-backed, fleet and instant schedules all fail on their earnings and trip floors; the express schedule fails because 492.56 is below its earnings floor of 500.00; the weekly batch schedule asks 3 settled trips and 30 days of tenure and both are met. Any agent who measures the three figures the way the rule states converges on that one name.

edges.condition: Every entry on the account that has left it short of money the marketplace is owed is answered by a recovery entry taken against it.
edges.policy_source: The schedule a host moves onto is settled only once every ground on which the account stands short of money the marketplace is owed carries the recovery entry taken against it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-09-17 the ledger carries a chargeback of 4820.00 booked on 2026-09-08 on the chargeback recovery basis, and no entry anywhere on the account names it through source_ledger_id, so no recovery has been taken against it; the account's own available balance of -1310.00 shows the shortfall still standing, and it is exactly the netting of the ledger behind it. The deductions and corrections of the twelve months therefore come to -6000.00 rather than -7703.00, and the qualifying monthly earnings to 506.75 rather than 492.56.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The deduction of 1703.00 booked at step 7 is taken against that chargeback and names it, so the account no longer stands short without a recovery; the twelve-month flows fall to -7703.00, the qualifying monthly earnings to 492.56, and the schedule settled recomputes from the Keyturn Express Payout Schedule to the Keyturn Weekly Batch Payout Schedule.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a two-node chain with a single edge, so there is no pair of prerequisites that could be reordered at all: the schedule settled at step 9 reads the twelve-month flows that the recovery at step 7 writes into.
